You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

6 5 5
5 1 7
4 5 2

Output 5x5. Each input cell maps to a block? 3x3 cells -> block sizes? Row blocks: sizes 2,1,2? Rows of output: rows 1-2 = row1, row3 = row2, rows 4-5 = row3. So row block heights = [2,1,2]. Column blocks: cols 1-2 (width 2), col3 (width1), cols4-5 (width2) -> [2,1,2].

Each cell value expanded into its block. Check: cell(1,1)=6 -> 2x2 block of 6. cell(1,2)=5 -> 2x1 block of 5s. cell(1,3)=5 -> 1x2? Output row1: 6 6 5 5 5 — cols4-5 are 5,5. Cell (1,3)=5 -> block 2 wide, height 2. Yes.

But blocks sized how? Maybe block size depends on cell value? Block heights: rows corresponding to input row i. Input row counts: row1 = [6,5,5], row2=[5,1,7], row3=[4,5,2]. Hmm heights [2,1,2], widths [2,1,2].

Maybe size = number of occurrences of that value in grid? Counts: 5 appears 4, 6 appears 1... no.

Maybe size related to something per row/column. Height 2 for row1 and row3, 1 for row2. Width 2 for col1 and col3, 1 for col2. Symmetric. Maybe block size = count of that value in its row? Row1: values 6,5,5. Widths per column: col1 block width 2, col2 width1, col3 width2. Hmm.

Alternative: maybe size = number of times the value appears in the whole grid? 5 appears 4 times... no, 5-block is 2 wide.

Maybe size = count of that value in the column/row? Column1: 6,5,4 all distinct. Hmm.

Maybe size relates to the cell's position parity? Positions 1,3 -> size 2; position 2 -> size 1. So odd indices get 2, even get 1? All consistent: height = 2 if row index odd else 1; width = 2 if col index odd else 1.
